ruleName: Actions Affecting Ball on Putting Green
imagePrompt: Create a polished, modern semi-realistic illustration (about 75% realistic, 25% stylised) in the established junior golf quiz style. Show a golfer on a putting green in mid-follow-through from a practice swing with a putter, clearly having accidentally struck a golf ball, which is now shown several feet away from its original spot. Make the setting clearly a putting green with a visible flag in the hole in the background, lush green surfaces, and gentle undulations. Ensure the situation is clear but do not include text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards, or speech bubbles.
imageAlt: A golfer on the putting green has just hit their golf ball by accident during a practice swing. The golf ball is now sitting several feet from where it was, and the flagstick can be seen in the hole.

sceneSpec.setting: Putting green on a golf course with a visible flagstick and surround.
sceneSpec.players: One golfer standing on the putting green having just made a practice swing. The golfer is holding a putter. No other players are visible.
sceneSpec.ballPosition: A golf ball that has been accidentally struck by the putter and has rolled several feet away from its original location on the green.
sceneSpec.ruleMoment: The moment immediately after the practice swing, with the player's putter shown in follow-through and the ball at rest a short distance from its original position.
sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Illustrate that accidentally moving the ball on the green during a practice swing results in no penalty, but the ball must be replaced.
mustShow: Golfer with putter (in post-practice swing pose)
Golf ball at rest away from its original spot on the putting green
Flagstick in the background to establish the location as a putting green

questions.title: Practice Swing Accidentally Moves Your Ball on the Green
questions.question: Your ball is sitting on the green. Before you putt, you take a practice swing, but you accidentally hit your ball and it rolls away. What should you do?

choices.text: This counts as your next shot. Play from where the ball stops.
You get one penalty stroke and put the ball back where it was.
There is no penalty. Put the ball back where it was before you hit it.
There is no penalty. Play the ball from where it rolled to.

questions.explanation: Because you didn’t mean to hit your ball with your practice swing, you don’t get a penalty. Just put your ball back in its old spot and then play your putt.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The short grass around the hole where you use your putter.
A swing you make to get ready, but not to hit the ball.

questions.teachingTip: Practising by swinging next to your ball is normal, just try to be careful not to touch your ball. If it does move, remember you won’t get a penalty on the green, but you must put it back.
likelyMisconceptions: Some children might think any hit counts as a stroke, even if it’s an accident.
Some children may think you always get a penalty if the ball is moved, even on the green.

questions.title: Practice Swing Moves Ball on Putting Green
questions.question: Your ball is on the putting green. Before making your putt, you take a practice swing and accidentally hit the ball, causing it to roll several feet away. What is the correct ruling?

choices.text: Count it as your next stroke and play the ball from where it came to rest.
You receive a one-stroke penalty and must replace the ball.
There is no penalty. Replace the ball on its original spot before making your stroke.
There is no penalty. Play the ball from where it came to rest.

questions.explanation: A practice swing is not a stroke as there was no intention to hit the ball. On the putting green, if a player accidentally causes their ball to move, there is no penalty. The ball must be replaced on its original spot before making the next stroke (Rule 13.1d(1)).
